categories.title: Data honesty
categories.blurb: The number is what it says it is, and the reader can tell where it came from.

categories.title: Encoding and chart choice
categories.blurb: The mark matches the relationship, and the chart does not hide a simpler reading.

categories.title: Colour and legibility
categories.blurb: Colour carries meaning without becoming the only carrier, in light and dark mode.

categories.title: Accessibility
categories.blurb: A screen reader, keyboard, or low-vision reader can reach the same finding.

categories.title: Layout and responsiveness
categories.blurb: The chart survives narrow screens, zoom, loading, and print without losing labels.

categories.title: States and failure
categories.blurb: Empty, partial, stale, flat, and broken data each get a state a reader can understand.

categories.title: Narrative and context
categories.blurb: The title, note, and surrounding text state the finding and the limits of the data.

categories.title: Interaction, animation and 3D
categories.blurb: Exploratory views stay operable, understandable, and still when the reader asks.

categories.title: Maps and spatial views
categories.blurb: Geography carries values without hiding scale, vintage, coverage, or missing areas.

categories.title: Process and delivery
categories.blurb: Every chart has an owner, an evidence trail, and a check that runs before release.

rules.title: Name the measure, geography, and period
rules.check: The subtitle or deck names the measure, the geography, and the period.
rules.fix: Add the missing element. Put the measure first, then the place, then the dates.

rules.title: Put units on every quantitative value
rules.check: Every quantitative axis, tooltip, and value label carries its unit. Categorical axes are exempt.
rules.fix: Add the unit once to the axis title and to each tooltip or label that stands alone.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist

rules.title: Show the source and as-of date
rules.check: The chart shows its source and as-of date, or links to a source block in the same section with both fields.
rules.fix: Add a source line with the publisher, dataset, and date. Link to the fuller source block when one exists.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist

rules.title: Start bars and areas at zero
rules.check: Bars and areas have a zero baseline.
rules.fix: Set the value axis minimum to zero for bar and area marks, or change to a mark that can crop.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist

rules.title: Label a cropped axis and leave room before the first point
rules.check: A cropped line or scatter axis states its actual domain and leaves a gap of 25% to 33% of plot height or width before the first point.
rules.fix: Show the axis start value and add the gap. If the crop changes the reading, use zero instead.

rules.title: Remove the reader-facing second y-axis
rules.check: No chart asks the reader to interpret two y-axes. A rendering helper with no second scale needs a recorded exception.
rules.fix: Split into two charts, index both series to a common base, or label the secondary series directly without a second axis.

rules.title: State the denominator or population base
rules.check: A rate states its denominator. A place comparison states the population base.
rules.fix: Add the denominator to the subtitle, note, or tooltip. Name the population and the year.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Statistical disclosure control for tables
Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Suppress cells below the publisher threshold
rules.check: A cell below the publisher disclosure threshold is suppressed. The threshold belongs to the source. Where none is given, the default is 5.
rules.fix: Apply the source threshold. If the publisher gives none, suppress cells under 5 and state the rule.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Statistical disclosure control for tables
Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Show published uncertainty where it changes the reading
rules.check: Uncertainty appears when the source publishes it. Bars do not use error bars. A dot plot with ranges or a line with a band is used instead.
rules.fix: Add a range, band, or interval and explain it in plain words. Keep error bars off bar and column marks.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist
Weissgerber et al.: Small-sample data visualisation

rules.title: Keep rounding within source precision
rules.check: Displayed values do not exceed source precision, and displayed totals agree within half of the last displayed digit.
rules.fix: Round to the source precision. Recompute totals from the rounded values or add a rounding note.

rules.title: Explain a non-zero baseline
rules.check: A line or scatter chart with a non-zero baseline states why zero was not used.
rules.fix: Add one sentence to the note or subtitle that names the reason for the crop.

rules.title: Distinguish missing periods from assumptions
rules.check: Missing periods render as a gap or a dashed assumed segment. Observations are visually distinct from assumptions.
rules.fix: Use a gap for missing data and a dashed segment for an assumption. Add a legend or note for the dash.

sources.title: Datawrapper: Missing data in line charts

rules.title: Declare the relationship and match the chart type
rules.check: The chart declares one relationship from the controlled list, and the rendered chart type appears in that relationship row.
rules.fix: Add the relationship from docs/relationship-map.md to the chart metadata. Change the chart type or record an exception with a reason and a link.

rules.title: Use position or length for precise comparison
rules.check: Position or length carries the value when a precise comparison matters. No 3D and no area for precise ranking.
rules.fix: Replace angle, area, or 3D encoding with a bar, dot, or line. Keep decoration out of the data mark.

rules.title: Declare the order and render it
rules.check: The chart declares its order as value, natural, or alphabetical, and the rendered order matches the declaration.
rules.fix: Set the declared sort in the chart config. If the order is editorial, name the rule in the note.

rules.title: Keep categorical series to five or fewer
rules.check: A chart has five or fewer categorical series. Six or seven need a recorded exception. More than seven fails.
rules.fix: Group small series into Other, use small multiples, or let the reader filter. Record any exception.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist

rules.title: Label four or fewer series directly
rules.check: Four or fewer series are labelled beside the marks instead of through a legend.
rules.fix: Place the series name at the end of each line or beside each group. Remove the legend when no longer needed.

rules.title: Label a log scale and state its base
rules.check: A log scale is labelled as logarithmic and states its base.
rules.fix: Add the scale name and base to the axis title or note. Use a linear scale when the log does not help.

rules.title: Compare like with like
rules.check: Comparisons use the same period, definition, and denominator on both sides.
rules.fix: Align the periods and definitions. If they differ, state the difference and why the comparison still holds.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist

rules.title: Cite the source for event annotations
rules.check: Annotations for known events cite the event source.
rules.fix: Add the source and date to the annotation or its footnote.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Offer a simpler alternative for a hard chart type
rules.check: A chart type that is hard to read has a simpler alternative, such as a table or bar view.
rules.fix: Add a table view, a bar toggle, or a short summary that carries the same comparison.

rules.title: Keep pie and doughnut slices honest
rules.check: A pie or doughnut sums to 100% within rounding, has no negative values, and has five or fewer slices.
rules.fix: Use a bar chart, group small slices into Other, or remove the pie when the parts do not sum to a whole.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist

rules.title: Match data density to the question
rules.check: Data density suits the question. Individual labels are limited to 20 marks, and a dense chart offers aggregation, a filter, or a table.
rules.fix: Reduce marks, aggregate, add a filter, or provide a table. Keep the chart focused on one comparison.

rules.title: Keep grouped bars to four categories
rules.check: A clustered or stacked bar has four or fewer categories per group.
rules.fix: Split the chart, group small categories, or switch to small multiples.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist

rules.title: Share scales across small multiples
rules.check: Small multiples share scale, order, and colour meaning, and the shared scale is labelled once.
rules.fix: Set one domain per measure, keep the same series order, and label the shared axis or legend.

rules.title: Keep chart text at 12px or larger
rules.check: All rendered chart text is at least 12 CSS pixels, about 9 points.
rules.fix: Raise the font size in the chart theme and the SVG text rule. Recheck at 320px.

rules.title: Meet text contrast ratios
rules.check: Text meets 4.5:1 contrast, or 3:1 at 24px and above, or 18.66px bold and above.
rules.fix: Change the text or background token until the ratio passes in light and dark mode.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Data visualisation colours in charts

rules.title: Meet 3:1 for marks against adjacent colours
rules.check: Data marks meet 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours and the background.
rules.fix: Darken or lighten the mark, add a boundary, or change the adjacent fill.

rules.title: Separate touching fills
rules.check: Touching fills have a 1px separator or a 3:1 boundary.
rules.fix: Add a background-coloured stroke or increase the contrast between the fills.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Data visualisation colours in charts

rules.title: Never use colour as the only channel
rules.check: Colour is not the only channel. Texture, shape, dash, or a direct label carries the same meaning.
rules.fix: Add a second channel to every series or category, and check it in grayscale.

rules.title: Check the palette under colour vision deficiency
rules.check: The palette survives protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia, and achromatopsia simulation with distinguishable lightness.
rules.fix: Change the palette to vary lightness as well as hue. Avoid red-green and yellow-blue pairs.

rules.title: Use sequential and diverging palettes only for ordered data
rules.check: Sequential and diverging palettes are used only for ordered data. Categorical data uses a categorical palette.
rules.fix: Swap the palette to a categorical set, or reorder the data if the sequence is real.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Data visualisation colours in charts

rules.title: Repeat contrast checks in dark mode
rules.check: C2 and C3 pass again in dark mode. Text passes through axe and marks pass the token contrast test.
rules.fix: Add dark tokens for text, gridlines, marks, and focus. Run the same contrast checks in both themes.

sources.title: Datawrapper: Dark mode in embedded visualisations

rules.title: Survive forced-colors and high contrast
rules.check: Windows high contrast and forced-colors keep marks, labels, and focus visible.
rules.fix: Use system colours or forced-colors fallbacks for marks, text, and focus. Test with forced colors enabled.

rules.title: Use round, labelled gridlines
rules.check: Gridlines are round-numbered and labelled, with no minor gridlines. Use 6 to 10 on desktop and 3 to 6 on mobile.
rules.fix: Set the tick count and round the domain. Remove minor gridlines and lighten the remaining lines.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist

rules.title: Avoid flashing and red large-area animation
rules.check: Nothing flashes more than three times per second, and no animation uses red as a large-area flash.
rules.fix: Remove the flash, lower the frequency, or replace the animation with a static state change.

rules.title: Use shared tokens and components
rules.check: Colours, type scale, and interaction patterns come from shared tokens and components. Chart code has no hard-coded values.
rules.fix: Move the value into a token or shared chart theme, then replace the local constant.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Give the chart an image role and a short name
rules.check: The chart has an image role and a short accessible name.
rules.fix: Add role="img" and a name through aria-label or aria-labelledby. Keep the name short and specific.

rules.title: State the finding in the accessible name and visible text
rules.check: The accessible name states the finding, and a visible sentence states the same takeaway without requiring the chart.
rules.fix: Write one sentence with the finding. Use it for the visible summary and the accessible description.

rules.title: Provide a data table with the same values
rules.check: A data table carries the same values, units, and series order as the chart, with a caption and header cells.
rules.fix: Add a caption, column headers, and every series in chart order. Keep the table in the DOM or behind a clear link.

rules.title: Make every interactive feature keyboard operable
rules.check: Every interactive feature is reachable and operable with the keyboard, with no keyboard trap.
rules.fix: Use native controls where possible. Add key handlers for custom marks and a way out of every interaction.

rules.title: Keep focus visible and unobscured
rules.check: Focus is not obscured, and the indicator is at least 2px with 3:1 contrast against its background.
rules.fix: Add a visible focus ring to every chart control. Remove overlays that cover the focused element.

rules.title: Keep non-interactive marks out of the tab order
rules.check: Non-interactive marks are not in the tab order.
rules.fix: Remove tabindex from decorative and static marks. Put one tab stop on the chart, not on every mark.

rules.title: Announce tooltips and status changes
rules.check: Tooltip and status changes are announced in a live region.
rules.fix: Add a polite live region for the active value and for loading, error, and update messages.

rules.title: Let the reader reduce motion
rules.check: Interaction-triggered motion can be reduced, and autoplaying animation over five seconds can be paused, stopped, or hidden.
rules.fix: Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Add pause and stop controls for any animation over five seconds.

rules.title: Explain the purpose and the controls
rules.check: Interaction instructions are visible, name the keyboard controls, and state what the chart is for.
rules.fix: Add a short instruction line beside the chart. Name the keys and the action they perform.

rules.title: Keep no value or comparison on hover alone
rules.check: No value or comparison exists only on hover.
rules.fix: Show key values in labels, the table, or a pinned detail panel. Treat hover as an extra.

sources.title: Datawrapper: Accessible charts, maps and tables

rules.title: Make changed state reproducible
rules.check: A changed state from filters or hidden series can be reproduced from the URL or a visible description.
rules.fix: Write filter state to the URL or show a short state summary the reader can copy.

rules.title: Do not override assistive technology settings
rules.check: Custom keyboard and touch controls do not override screen-reader or browser settings, and apply only while the chart has focus.
rules.fix: Scope key handlers to the focused chart. Do not capture global keys or block browser zoom and scroll.

rules.title: Use one tab stop for dense charts
rules.check: A chart with more than 50 marks exposes one tab stop and reveals detail with arrow keys. Every mark is not a tab stop.
rules.fix: Make the chart one focusable group. Move detail with arrow keys and announce the active mark.

rules.title: Survive text spacing and font overrides
rules.check: Text spacing overrides and user font settings do not clip labels or hide data.
rules.fix: Let labels wrap or move. Avoid fixed-height text boxes and fixed-width axis gutters.

rules.title: Avoid horizontal scroll at 320px
rules.check: The chart container causes no horizontal scroll at 320 CSS pixels, equivalent to 400% zoom at 1280px.
rules.fix: Let the chart shrink, stack controls, or move the table below. Remove fixed pixel widths from the figure.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Keep labels unclipped at three widths
rules.check: Labels are not clipped or overlapped at 320px, 768px, and 1280px.
rules.fix: Shorten labels, wrap them, move them to a direct label, or increase the axis gutter.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Keep pointer targets at 24px or larger
rules.check: Interactive targets are at least 24px, with 44px preferred.
rules.fix: Increase the hit area without enlarging the visible mark. Keep spacing between adjacent targets.

rules.title: Reserve chart height before hydration
rules.check: The chart container reserves its height before hydration, and the measured height does not shift after hydration.
rules.fix: Set an aspect ratio or min-height on the figure. Render a skeleton with the same height.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Lazy-load charts below the first viewport
rules.check: A chart below the first viewport is lazy loaded, and its request starts after the first viewport renders.
rules.fix: Load the chart component and data near the viewport. Keep the hero chart eager.

rules.title: Keep the chart in print
rules.check: The printed page keeps the chart, its title, and its source.
rules.fix: Add print styles for the figure. Avoid hiding the chart behind an interaction that print cannot reach.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Survive 200% text zoom
rules.check: The chart survives 200% text zoom without losing labels.
rules.fix: Use relative text sizes and flexible gutters. Let labels wrap or move to a second line.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Keep reading order with the visual order
rules.check: When the chart stacks at narrow widths, the visual order still matches the DOM order.
rules.fix: Change the DOM order before using CSS order. Put the title, chart, note, and table in the order a reader needs.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Explain an empty dataset
rules.check: An empty dataset renders an explanation, not an empty box.
rules.fix: Show a short message with the reason and the next step. Keep the chart title and source visible.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Name the source and retry path on failure
rules.check: A fetch failure names the source and the retry path.
rules.fix: Show the source name, a plain error, and a retry control. Announce the change in a live region.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Render a single data point clearly
rules.check: A single data point renders and says there is one point.
rules.fix: Draw the point and add a note that the chart has one observation. Do not imply a trend.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Give a flat series an explicit domain
rules.check: An all-zero or flat series gets an explicit domain instead of a collapsed axis.
rules.fix: Set a sensible domain and label it. Add a note when every value is the same.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: State when outliers are excluded
rules.check: Outlier handling is stated when points are excluded.
rules.fix: Add the exclusion rule to the note and link to the full data when possible.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Mark stale and partial data
rules.check: Stale or partial data carries its as-of date and states what is missing.
rules.fix: Add the date and the missing period or region. Keep the label beside the chart, not only in a tooltip.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Handle extreme values without clipping
rules.check: Maximum, minimum, negative, and very large values do not clip or overlap.
rules.fix: Test the extremes, pad the domain, and move labels away from the plot edge.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Separate no data, zero, and missing
rules.check: No data, a true zero, and a missing value are visually and textually distinct.
rules.fix: Use a distinct empty state, a zero mark, and a gap or dash for missing. Explain each in the key.

sources.title: Datawrapper: Missing data in line charts
Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: State the finding in the title
rules.check: The title states the finding, not the variable name.
rules.fix: Rewrite the title as a sentence with the subject and the change. Keep it under 15 words.

rules.title: Explain what the chart is for
rules.check: A short note explains what the chart is for and how to read it, in plain language.
rules.fix: Add two or three sentences beside the chart. Name the comparison and the one thing to notice.

rules.title: Keep chart text at grade 9 or lower
rules.check: Chart text reads at grade 9 or lower on a Flesch-Kincaid check.
rules.fix: Shorten sentences, remove jargon, and split long labels. Re-run the readability check.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Do not imply causation without support
rules.check: No causal claim appears unless the source supports it.
rules.fix: Replace causal verbs with neutral ones. State the confounder or drop the claim.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Answer the question the page asks
rules.check: The chart answers the question the page asks.
rules.fix: Re-read the page heading and the chart. Remove the chart or change the measure if they answer different questions.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Give every 3D or interactive view a non-visual equivalent
rules.check: Every 3D or interactive view has a table, text summary, or 2D fallback that carries the same values and relationships.
rules.fix: Add a table or a written finding beside the view. Keep the fallback reachable without the canvas.

rules.title: Give every pointer action a keyboard path
rules.check: Every action available by pointer has a keyboard path. No action is drag-only or hover-only.
rules.fix: Add buttons or key handlers for rotate, pan, zoom, select, and reset. Keep the pointer path as an extra.

rules.title: Expose the active state of controls
rules.check: Toggles, layers, and tools expose their active state through aria-pressed, aria-selected, or a visible state that matches the DOM.
rules.fix: Set the state attribute and keep it in sync with the scene. Do not rely on a colour change alone.

rules.title: Describe and reproduce the current view
rules.check: The current camera, section, layer, and selection are described in text and can be reproduced from the URL or a visible summary.
rules.fix: Write the view state to the URL or a state panel. Give a reset control a stable default.

rules.title: Respect reduced motion in the scene
rules.check: Camera motion and auto-rotation respect prefers-reduced-motion, and no view moves without a reader action unless it can be paused.
rules.fix: Disable auto-rotation under reduced motion. Add pause and reset controls to every moving scene.

rules.title: Announce loading and keep the page usable
rules.check: Loading and progress messages are announced, and a heavy scene does not block the first content or the page controls.
rules.fix: Show a status message, reserve the scene area, and load models or tiles after the page shell renders.

rules.title: Keep labels legible and controllable
rules.check: Labels and annotations remain legible at every zoom level and can be toggled off.
rules.fix: Scale or reposition labels, avoid overlap, and add a label toggle that also works from the keyboard.

rules.title: Name layer, region, and search controls
rules.check: Layer, region, and search controls have accessible names, grouped semantics, and a visible count where the set changes.
rules.fix: Use fieldset and legend or a labelled group. Name each control and announce the visible count.

rules.title: Give spatial views an orientation aid
rules.check: A spatial view shows orientation through an axis gizmo, overview, breadcrumb, or named view presets.
rules.fix: Add a small orientation control and a reset. Name the current view in text.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Set a frame-rate and asset budget
rules.check: The scene meets a recorded frame-rate and asset budget on a mid-range device, and the measured numbers are written down.
rules.fix: Measure on a mid-range phone. Reduce model size, draw distance, or effects until the budget holds.

rules.title: Give the map a text equivalent
rules.check: A map has a text alternative or data table that carries the same values. The map is not the only route to the data.
rules.fix: Add a table, a ranked list, or a written summary beside the map. Keep the same values and geography.

rules.title: State the projection, extent, and scale
rules.check: The map states its projection, geographic extent, and scale or a scale bar.
rules.fix: Add the projection and extent to the note. Add a scale bar when distance matters.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Explain the map legend and units
rules.check: The legend explains the colour or size encoding and its units.
rules.fix: Add a labelled legend with units and the class breaks or size scale.

sources.title: GOV.UK Analysis Function: Charts, a checklist

rules.title: Show boundary and geometry vintage
rules.check: The boundary or geometry vintage and its source are shown.
rules.fix: Add the boundary year and source to the source line. Date any geometry that changes.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Do not rely on colour alone on a map
rules.check: Map classes are not carried by colour alone. Patterns, labels, boundaries, or values provide a second channel.
rules.fix: Add a pattern, a boundary, a label, or a value to every class. Check the map in grayscale.

rules.title: Distinguish missing areas from zero
rules.check: Missing or unreliable areas have a distinct treatment from areas with a true zero.
rules.fix: Use a separate fill or hatch for missing areas and name it in the legend.

sources.title: Datawrapper: Missing data in line charts
Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Make zoom and pan keyboard accessible
rules.check: Zoom and pan work from the keyboard, a reset control is present, and the map has no keyboard trap.
rules.fix: Add zoom buttons, arrow-key pan, and a reset. Keep the map focusable only while it is active.

rules.title: Offer a small-screen text view
rules.check: On small screens, the map offers a list or table view that does not require zooming or panning.
rules.fix: Add a table or ranked list tab. Keep the map as the visual overview.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: List every chart instance with an owner
rules.check: Every rendered chart has an inventory entry with its page, component, owner, and chart family.
rules.fix: Add the chart to the project inventory. Fail the build when a chart component has no entry.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Capture visual snapshots at three widths
rules.check: A visual snapshot exists at 320px, 768px, and 1280px in light and dark mode for every chart that changes appearance.
rules.fix: Add the visual test and store baselines from a fixed CI image, not a developer laptop.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Run axe on every chart page
rules.check: axe runs on every page with a chart and returns zero serious or critical violations.
rules.fix: Add axe to the page test. Fix serious and critical violations before release.

rules.title: Keep a current manual audit
rules.check: The manual audit for the chart family is newer than the rendering code and no more than 12 months old.
rules.fix: Re-audit the family when the rendering code changes or the audit expires. Record the date and auditor.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Regenerate the audit report
rules.check: The audit report is regenerated when the gate runs, so its rows match the current inventory.
rules.fix: Generate the report in the gate. Fail when the committed report differs from the generated one.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.

rules.title: Record a verdict for every rule and chart
rules.check: The report has one row per chart per rule. A blank row counts as a failure.
rules.fix: Record pass, fail, or not applicable with evidence. Do not leave a row blank.

sources.title: Chart Checklist house rule
sources.note: No external source. This checklist sets a project default.
